title: Rare Diseases, Common Dilemmas: LLMs Prioritize Equal Resource Distribution over Patient Benefit in Decision-Making

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM responses to forced-choice clinical vignettes to determine if ethical value selections shift depending on whether the decision-maker is framed as an institutional committee, a medical team, or an individual patient.

Measuring the normalized win rates of core bioethical principles (Justice, Autonomy, Beneficence, Non-maleficence) to detect systemic preferences for specific moral frameworks, such as equal resource distribution, over others.
Testing the statistical association (using Cramér's V) between patient age categories (Infant, Pediatric, Adult) embedded in clinical vignettes and the ethical values prioritized by the LLMs.
Analyzing the association between patient decisional ability contexts (Maternal-Fetal, Proxy, Self-Directed) and the resulting ethical value choices made by the LLMs.
